task_brief: Day 4 of "Debugging, Testing, and Version Control" (unit 3, grade 9) is a build and test on test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 45–75 minutes. The unit is working toward: Repair a supplied defective program and deliver a commit history, a defect log, a failing test that reproduces the bug, and a verified fix. Today's work contributes to that by handling test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling at the application or project stage, against the unit's wider topics of defect classes and error messages, reading traces and diagnostic output, systematic debugging strategy, and version control commits and history. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Build a working artifact for a stated need arising in the unit "Debugging, Testing, and Version Control", built around what this session covers: test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling. Write the requirements and the success conditions first, in testable form, before writing the artifact. Then implement it, run it against at least three cases — a normal case, a boundary case, and a case designed to break it — and log actual versus expected for each. Fix every failing case and re-run. Submit the artifact, the test log, and a short design note explaining one alternative you rejected and why. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling, and it belongs to "Debugging, Testing, and Version Control", which also covers separate topics such as defect classes and error messages. Close out with this check before you stop: Show this session’s increment and name what remains before the task is complete. At grade 9 the bar is independent work with explicit criteria set before you start, and evidence that you evaluated the finished result against those criteria rather than against how it felt.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

remediation: Reteaching for test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling, model it in a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the approach to test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "requests the answer to graded work": Explain the concept, ask a diagnostic question, or help isolate the defect. Do not supply the graded artifact, solution code, or finished creative work. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking test case design and edge cases and assertions and defensive input handling mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
